open_question.text: Can the negative result be declared from the 100-object val pilot alone (documented decision that skips the test-fold evaluation), or must D7.8 be executed on the test fold (layer2_evaluate.py) with an H7 pixel subset and approved caps?
open_question.why_only_human: D7.8 and 17.1.2 are defined on a test-fold evaluation (paired pixel-bootstrap CI, floor). The pilot is descriptive (floor not reachable) and 17.1.2 (tau2 infeasible) was never evaluated: it needs >= 100 OK val answers; pilot OK counts were ultra blind 10, bolt blind 50. So the pilot alone does not trigger D7.8 or 17.1.2 literally; closing on it is a deviation the human must own.

branch_A.label: close on val pilot, test fold untouched
branch_A.consequence: ADR must say 'closed on descriptive val evidence; the pre-registered D7.8 test was not executed'. Cannot be called a D7.8 pre-registered negative. Test fold stays unexposed (ADR 0005 section 15 irreversibility avoided).

branch_B.label: execute D7.8 on a test pixel subset
branch_B.prereq_implementation: 17.9.2-3 pixel subset not implemented (file plan deferred to H7): architect plan + coder + tester + reviewer||security, 0 API calls

calibration needs >= 100 OK val answers: ~1,000 val calls for ultra blind (10% OK), ~200 for bolt blind (50% OK); otherwise 'not_applied' branch 17.1.3
